rendering.persona_description: Lucía is a 52-year-old school office administrator who has lived in the same small town for most of her adult life. She's known among coworkers for being organized and reliable, the one who keeps everyone else on schedule. Outside work she likes gardening and used to do more hiking before she started avoiding anything that raised her heart rate.
rendering.clinical_context: Lucía has health anxiety centered on cardiac symptoms; she became fixated three years ago after a heart palpitation episode that turned out to be benign, and has since interpreted normal bodily sensations (racing heart, chest tightness, dizziness) as signs of an undetected heart problem despite repeated normal cardiac workups. She tried a course of exposure-based treatment about two years ago but stopped after a few months, feeling it wasn't worth the discomfort it caused her week to week, and has not been in any treatment since.
rendering.behavioral_description: Lucía is polite and a little deferential, tends to agree with suggestions in the moment even when she has doubts, and rarely pushes back directly. She often circles back to describe a physical sensation in detail, asking indirectly whether it sounds serious, and will say she's 'probably fine' right after voicing the worry. She goes along with whatever is suggested to her but doesn't always follow through afterward, and tends to downplay how much the anxiety is still running her daily choices.

traits.living_situation: lives with her husband; two adult children live nearby
traits.communication_register: polite, mild, indirect; softens worries with hedges like 'it's probably nothing'
traits.help_seeking_orientation: seeks reassurance often, agrees readily with suggestions in the moment, but has not sought out structured treatment again since stopping a couple of years ago
traits.cognitive_style: catastrophizes bodily sensations, ruminates on medical possibilities, seeks certainty through checking and reassurance

clinical_history.presentation: health anxiety (illness anxiety) focused on fear of undetected heart disease
clinical_history.current_treatment: none currently; she is not in any treatment at this time
clinical_history.history: Symptoms began about three years ago after a palpitation episode with normal test results; anxiety has persisted despite reassurance from multiple cardiology evaluations. She began a course of exposure-based treatment about two and a half years ago but stopped after a few months, and has not returned to treatment since.

symptoms: monitors heart rate and chest sensations throughout the day
avoids exertion that raises heart rate, like hiking or climbing stairs quickly
seeks reassurance from doctors and family about symptoms
intrusive worry that a serious heart condition is being missed
physical tension and mild dizziness when anxious
difficulty concentrating at work when preoccupied with symptoms

affect.primary_emotion: worried, with an undertone of resignation that nothing has really helped
